_doc: jscpd (copy/paste detector) config for the DOCUMENTATION surface — bead sq-lrju. Consumed by the `docs-duplication (jscpd)` job in .github/workflows/docs-quality.yml, which is a HARD gate. WHY the doc surface and not code: prose has no compiler and no test to notice that two pages have drifted apart, so a copy/pasted paragraph is how a doc corpus silently grows two contradictory answers to the same question. The repo already prefers single-sourcing (book/src/**.md are {{#include}} wrappers over README/SKILL anchors) — this gate keeps that property from eroding rather than trying to earn it back later.
_doc_teeth: `threshold: 0` is the ONLY thing that makes this lane block. jscpd's `exitCode` defaults to 0, so finding clones is not by itself fatal; setting `threshold` makes jscpd append its `threshold` reporter, which throws (exit 1) as soon as the measured duplication percentage exceeds the threshold. Raise or remove `threshold` and the lane still runs, still prints every clone, and still exits 0 — a gate that reports and never blocks. scripts/tests/test_docs_duplication.sh case A' pins that.
_doc_allowlist: An INTENTIONAL repeat is allowlisted IN THE FILE, never by widening `threshold` or dropping a path from `path` — a repeat worth keeping is worth annotating with the reason it is deliberate. The markers MUST be written as markdown link-reference comments:  [//]: # (jscpd:ignore-start)  …  [//]: # (jscpd:ignore-end)  — each on its own line, blank-line separated. The obvious spelling, an HTML comment `<!-- jscpd:ignore-start -->`, DOES NOT WORK in markdown: jscpd injects its ignore grammar into every Prism language, but the markup grammar consumes `<!--` first and `jscpd:` comes back out as a `namespace` token, so the block is never ignored (verified against jscpd 4.0.5; pinned by test case C). That mis-spelling is fail-CLOSED — it leaves the gate red, never green — but it is confusing enough to be worth stating here. Put the human-readable REASON in an ordinary HTML comment next to the markers; see research/noir-acir-expression-growth-4629.md for the shape.
_doc_scope: path/ignore: the scoped doc corpus (root README + docs/ + skills/ + research/ + book/) minus the RENDERED mdBook output. `mdbook build book` writes book/book/, a rendered copy of book/src plus the README/SKILL anchors it {{#include}}s — i.e. duplicated by construction. It is gitignored (book/.gitignore) so it is absent on a clean CI checkout; the glob is belt-and-braces for a dirty tree, and it is written `**/book/book/**` rather than `book/book/**` because config-file `path` entries are resolved to ABSOLUTE paths before fast-glob sees them, which a repo-relative ignore glob would not match (test case D/D').
_doc_tuning: maxLines/maxSize are RAISED from the jscpd defaults (1000 lines / 100kb), which silently SKIPPED 10 markdown files totalling 12,634 lines of this corpus — including the largest and most duplication-prone pages (skills/http-server/SKILL.md is 1939 lines) — so the defaults would have left the gate blind exactly where it matters most. mode `strict` keeps comment/whitespace tokens in the comparison (it drops only `ignore` tokens), so a repeated block is detected even when only its prose is shared. minTokens 80 with minLines 5 is the sensitivity: it clears ordinary shared scaffolding (a heading plus a short table header) and catches a genuinely copy/pasted paragraph.
